## What do we think we know?

::: {.incremental}
- RT continuous
  - Bounded from below: $(0, RT_{max}]$^[The left parenthesis indicates we want to exclude zero; the right bracket indicates we want to include the maximum, but not anything above it.]
  - Or is there an $RT_{min}$?
- $RT_{congruent}<RT_{incongruent}$
- $Accuracy_{congruent}>Accuracy_{incongruent}$
:::

## {.center}

### In Bayesian statistics, these might be called *priors*. {style="text-align: center;"}

## Specify a model (in words)

- RT is equal to the time required to name a word's color
  - Plus more time if the color is...
  
## Specify a model (in words)

- RT is equal to the time required to name a word's color
  - Plus more time if the color is...**incongruent**
  
## Specify a model (in words)

- RT is equal to the time required to name a word's color
  - Plus more time if the color is...**incongruent**
  - Plus random error

## Specify a model (quantitatively)

::: {.incremental}
- Time to name a word's color: $RT_{name-a-color}$
- Extra time if the color is incongruent: $t_{incongruent}$
- Random error: $N(0, sd)$^[Random normal with some standard deviation, *sd*]

:::

::: {.fragment}
$$ RT=RT_{name-a-color}+t_{incongruent}+N(0, sd)$$
:::

## More (simplifying) assumptions

::: {.incremental}
- $RT_{name-a-color}$ is the same for all colors
- $RT_{name-a-color}$ doesn't change across the experiment
- $t_{incongruent}$ doesn't change across the experiment

:::

## How many congruent vs. incongruent trials?

- Let's specify 3/4 trials will be *congruent*
- Make attending to color of text more salient


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
congruency <- rep(c("cong", "cong", "cong", "incong"), 25)
cong_incong <- sample(x = congruency, replace = FALSE)
stroop_df$cong_incong <- cong_incong
```
:::

## On to our model

$$ RT=RT_{name-a-color}+t_{incongruent}+N(0, sd)$$


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
rt_name_a_color <- 500 # milliseconds
t_incong <- 20
sd_rt <- 10

stroop_df <- stroop_df |>
  mutate(rt = rt_name_a_color + 
           if_else(cong_incong == "incong", t_incong, 0) +
           rnorm(n = 100, sd = sd_rt))
```
:::


## How'd we do?


::: {.cell output-location='slide'}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
stroop_df |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = rt, 
                     fill = cong_incong), bins = 20)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](include/fig/fig-stroop-histogram-1.png){#fig-stroop-histogram width=960}
:::
:::

## Effect size

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- The "effect" of some manipulation
- In standard deviation units
- So, $\frac{t_{incong}}{sd_{rt}}$
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
| $t_{incong}$  | $sd_{rt}$ | effect size |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| 20        | 10    | 2           |
| 10        | 10    | 1           |
| 5         | 10    | 0.5         |
| 2.5       | 10    | 0.25        |
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
## Critique

- This simulation only projects a single year's data, not the time series reported in the survey.
- To depict changes over time, we'd need to specify about how *p*(wrong_track) changes over time.
- *p*(wrong_track) + *p*(right_track) + *p*(not_sure) must always = 1.
:::

## Why should we care about simulation?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Simulate your design before you collect data
- What is the data picture you expect?
- Build your data viz pipeline in advance
- Specify your assumptions, check them
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
- Build your *data analysis* pipeline in advance
- Simulation cheaper than running a study
- "Don't fool yourself because you are the easiest one to fool."
- "All models are wrong; some are useful."
:::
::::
